## About Me

Ph.D. Scholar in Electrical Engineering at **Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay**, specializing in Integrated Circuits and Systems (EE6). My research focuses on developing **resource-efficient on-chip classifiers for neural applications**, with emphasis on seizure detection and closed-loop neuromodulation.

## Research Work

### On-Chip Resource Efficient Classifiers for Neural Application | PhD Thesis
*Guide: Prof. Laxmeesha Somappa, Electrical Engineering, IIT Bombay (Jan'23 - present)*

**Completed Work:**

- Designed and architected a **16-channel logistic regression–based on-chip patient specific Seizure Detector** with an online retraining unit to enable adaptive closed-loop neuromodulation
- Developed a **shared multiply–accumulate (MAC) architecture** to reduce area and power while maintaining real-time throughput
- Completed the full **RTL-to-GDSII flow**, including RTL design, functional verification, synthesis, place-and-route, and sign-off

**Ongoing and Future Work:**

- Designing and training a **lightweight CNN architecture** for patient-independent Seizure Detection
- Exploring and modeling different **hardware accelerator architectures** for lightweight CNN models using SystemC
- Developing a **scalable CNN accelerator** capable of processing arbitrary CNN layers by integrating a PicoRV32 RISC-V processor
- Architecting the PicoRV32-based control subsystem to manage the accelerator datapath and memory system
- Executing the complete **RTL-to-GDSII physical design flow for TSMC 65nm node**

### Implementation of DFT in Quantum Computer | M.Tech
*Guide: Prof. Supratim Gupta, Electrical Engineering, NIT Rourkela (July'21 - June'22)*

- Developed an **FPGA-based emulator for quantum computing**, enabling the emulation of quantum algorithms
- Applied **Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT)-based methods** for quantum computation
